nodes.label: Patch Next.js Before Broader Work
nodes.rationale: Updating Next.js and eslint-config-next to 15.5.26 is prioritized because it is a small, isolated, verifiable change that follows an official out-of-band hardening recommendation.

nodes.label: Gouvernement du Québec Vehicle Purchase Guidance
nodes.norm_label: gouvernement du quebec vehicle purchase guidance

nodes.label: Pre-Screen Before Professional Inspection
nodes.rationale: Buyers often compare many listings and cannot justify a full mechanical inspection for every candidate, so a lower-cost pre-screen helps decide which vehicle deserves further attention.

nodes.label: Input Process Output Feedback Automation Map
nodes.norm_label: input process output feedback automation map

nodes.label: Initial Three-Offer Pricing Strategy
nodes.rationale: Three clear offers reduce early package confusion, while inspection fees should wait until partner operations and close rates are understood.

nodes.label: Manual Partner Dispatch for V1
nodes.rationale: Manual inspection dispatch is preferred until consistent demand and a reliable partner process justify automated scheduling.

nodes.label: Next.js App Router Selection
nodes.rationale: Next.js App Router was selected because the repository had no existing stack and the product plan prioritizes SEO, public pages, and evolution into a full web application.

nodes.label: Recommended Next.js Supabase Stripe Stack
nodes.rationale: Next.js supports the SEO-heavy public experience, Supabase covers core persistence and files, Stripe reduces payment complexity, Resend handles transactional delivery, and manual dispatch avoids premature scheduling complexity.

nodes.label: Two-Step AI Extraction and Report Workflow
nodes.norm_label: two-step ai extraction and report workflow

nodes.label: Report Safety and Non-Fabrication Rules
nodes.rationale: The report must distinguish visible risk from confirmed defects and must not fabricate accident, VIN, Carfax, lien, mechanical, pricing, honesty, legal, insurance, or official-status claims.

nodes.label: Launch Variant D Without Both Process Flags
nodes.norm_label: launch variant d without both process flags

nodes.label: Bounded Browser Disconnect Grace
nodes.rationale: A 75 ms bounded wait lets child-process exit and close events reach the failure snapshot.

nodes.label: Complete JSON Failure Logging
nodes.rationale: Serializing one complete JSON record keeps nested lifecycle and memory snapshots visible in Vercel logs instead of rendering them as Object placeholders.

nodes.label: Exact Browser Dependency Pinning
nodes.rationale: Exact pins prevent caret updates from silently separating Puppeteer's controller version from the deployed Chromium major version.

nodes.label: Explicit Null Cgroup Diagnostics
nodes.rationale: Unavailable cgroup metrics and memory.max=max are emitted as null rather than disappearing from JSON.

nodes.label: Literal Lazy Browser Imports
nodes.rationale: Literal package imports expose Puppeteer and Sparticuz dependency roots to Next.js output tracing while retaining lazy loading.

nodes.label: OOM Hypothesis Remains Unproven
nodes.rationale: Browser disconnection alone did not distinguish OOM, Chromium crash, or external termination.

nodes.label: Restore Sparticuz Graphics Default
nodes.rationale: The installed package's serverless graphics path uses ANGLE plus SwiftShader; disabling graphics produced an incompatible hybrid argument set.

nodes.label: Sequential Attempts Under Shared Deadline
nodes.rationale: Variants run one at a time under the original 25-second deadline and fully close before the next launch, preventing concurrent browsers.

nodes.label: Termination-Evidence-Only Matrix Fallback
nodes.rationale: The matrix advances only for launch failure or concrete browser-process/CDP termination, not for normal Facebook extraction, login, or deadline outcomes.

nodes.label: Post-Deployment Vercel Verification
nodes.rationale: Static and deterministic checks cannot prove the deployed Vercel browser behavior; one deployment and Marketplace request remain required.

nodes.label: Warm-Instance Successful Variant Retention
nodes.rationale: After a variant succeeds, later requests in the same warm Vercel instance launch only that proven variant.

nodes.label: Anonymous Facebook Access
nodes.rationale: The browser path intentionally avoids login, cookies, profiles, proxies, stealth, CAPTCHA solving, and access-control bypass.

nodes.label: No Unproven Resource Interception
nodes.rationale: Facebook scripts, styles, images, and fonts remain available because blocking them cannot be proven harmless to Marketplace rendering.

nodes.label: Render-Wait Scroll Pressure Reduction
nodes.rationale: Removing repeated bottom and top scrolling avoids unnecessary lazy Marketplace and recommendation rendering.

nodes.label: Zero-AI Deterministic Extraction
nodes.rationale: Listing URL and Facebook extraction remain deterministic and make no AI calls on the Free tier.
